name: route
description: Optional, and the one mod that needs an outside classifier model: hands feature and test work to delegate's cheaper worker. A fast classifier (TypeSafe's Jev or ScaleDown, with your API key) reads your prompt, and only where it is feature or test work does Claude get the order to implement it through a hand-off. Off until you turn it on and give it a key for one of them.

enabled.title: On
enabled.description: Off until you turn it on (here or in /mods): from then on the start of each prompt you send (up to 8,000 characters) goes to the classifier, a US service, to be classified.

classifier.title: Classifier
classifier.description: auto: TypeSafe's Jev when its key is set (0.25 s median, measured), else ScaleDown (1.15 s). Both were right on all 50 test prompts. TypeSafe keeps inputs as long as it needs them and never trains on them; ScaleDown's terms promise zero retention.

typesafeKey.title: TypeSafe API key
typesafeKey.description: For Jev. Else the TYPESAFE_API_KEY environment variable.

scaledownKey.title: ScaleDown API key
scaledownKey.description: Else the SCALEDOWN_API_KEY environment variable. The prompt's text is sent to ScaleDown (a US service) to be classified.

minScore.title: Hand off from (classifier score)
minScore.description: Only a prompt the classifier calls feature or test work with at least this score gets the order. 0: the classifier's own, measured on 877 real prompts: 0.95 for Jev (at 0.7 nearly half its hand-offs on one person's prompts were wrong), 0.7 for ScaleDown.

direct.title: Hand off before reading the code
direct.description: The order tells Claude to hand the work off at once and let the worker read the code, instead of looking around first. Measured (15 Oct): followed in 24 of 24 runs (looking around first, Opus kept the work in 5 of 16); 2 main-model requests on the TypeScript feature instead of 11 with the pack alone, all correct.
